newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- At least 35 royalist supporters held by forces of Cambodia's powerful Co-Premier Hun Sen have been executed, sources say as Hun Sen's troops make new territorial gains in northern Cambodia. King Norodom Sihanouk starts a series of meetings in Beijing with foreign envoys over the crisis. (BANGKOK POST)

- Police have charged an executive of the fire-gutted Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel with causing death and injury by negligence and have yet to decide whether to file charges against any of the eight others questioned. The cabinet has endorsed a National Safety Council proposal requiring local authorities to enforce building standards and make sure fire drills are held twice a year. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- The vetting panel has scored a major victory as the Constitution Drafting Assembly adopted the national party list system, but a question arises whether the New Aspiration Party will eventually approve the draft. The party list system is the first controversial point in the second reading of the Parliament chapter, which will directly affect MPs and senators who have authority to approve the draft. (THE NATION)

- Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya, Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanonda and Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn arrive in Tokyo today to seek continued Japanese investments to shore up the economy. They will also address Japanese monetary officials and bankers in Tokyo tomorrow explaining the Government's decision to manage float the baht. (BUSINESS DAY)

- More than 100 people have complained to the Commerce Ministry so far about manufacturers and distributors exploiting the depreciation of the baht by raising prices without justification. Products topping the list of complaints are wheat, aluminium, steel bars, plastic pellets, plastic bags, UHT milk, powdered milk, kraft paper, proof paper, latex and battery cells. (BANGKOK POST)

- Seafood canner Thai Union Frozen Plc will today make an announcement on its takeover of the third largest canned tuna producer in the United States, Van Camp Seafood Company Inc. The acquisition, worth over US$97 million, was made by Tri-Union Seafood LLC, an overseas subsidiary of Thailand's largest canned seafood producer. (THE NATION)
